h: Shabbos Brings Freedom and Joy to Every Jewish Soul

p: עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (תַּעֲנִית כט, ב)
This is based on what they said in the Gemara (Taanis 29b):
כְּרֵיחַ שָׂדֶה אֲשֶׁר בֵּרְכוֹ ה׳ (בְּרֵאשִׁית כז, כז)
"'Like the fragrance of a field which Hashem has blessed' (Bereishis 27:27)
like the fragrance of a field of apples";
the fragrance of Gan Eden entered with him;
this is what he said to him:
'See, the fragrance of my son is like the fragrance of a field'"
for Gan Eden is called the field of apples.
For the souls of Yisrael are called apples;
וְזֶה הָיָה בְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and this was so with Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
whose image was engraved on the Throne of Glory;
that is, he was like Adam HaRishon
"Let us make man in Our image, after Our likeness";
and he was in Gan Eden,
and Gan Eden the field of apples.
And so too Yisrael at the time of the Giving of the Torah,
שֶׁאָמַר לָהֶם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ (תְּהִלִּים פב, ו)
when Hashem Yisbarach said to them (Tehillim 82:6):
for then, were it not for the corruption,
הָיָה נִתְתַּקֵּן כָּל חֵטְא אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
the entire sin of Adam HaRishon would have been rectified,
so that they would not have died;
indeed, like Adam you shall die," etc. (Tehillim 82:7)
Therefore Yisrael were then likened to an apple,
when each one of Yisrael attains
דְּאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב פח, ב)
as is stated in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 88b):
"a soul in which there is all perfection,
after the pattern of the World to Come";
Shabbos is a semblance of the World to Come,
one sixtieth of the World to Come
so the souls of Yisrael too are called
And this meal the holy Arizal arranged
נֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
corresponding to the holiness of Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him.
וּבַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, חֵלֶק ג כט, א)
And in the holy Zohar (on this parsha, Zohar III 29a):
"And there is a cessation of work,
such as an ox that has a yoke
and a donkey that has a burden;
whether the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven,
בֵּין עוֹל מַלְכוּת עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
or the yoke of the kingdom of the idolaters,
they have cessation of work and repose."
the Kingdom of Heaven is called a yoke,
and also the yoke of mitzvos,
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עוֹל מִצְוֹת
"and afterward he accepts upon himself the yoke of mitzvos";
"Those who keep Shabbos shall rejoice in Your Kingship"
in accepting the yoke of His Kingship, may He be blessed,
and it is not called a yoke,
for then they have repose from it.
And one upon whom there is
the yoke of the kingdom of the idolaters
וּמִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם
and one who has the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven
"And those who occupy themselves with Torah and with the commandments
have the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven,
called the yoke of mitzvos," etc.
דְּעוֹל תּוֹרָה נִקְרָא גַּם כֵּן עוֹל
For the yoke of Torah is also called a yoke,
"Whoever accepts upon himself the yoke of Torah";
יָשִׂים אָדָם עַצְמוֹ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
"A person should set himself to words of Torah
like an ox to the yoke and like a donkey to the burden."
when words of Torah are called toil,
"He was created for the toil of Torah."
who toil in Torah during the week
for Hashem Yisbarach bestows upon them
And the holy Zohar further says:
all the creatures of heaven and earth, etc.;
That is, with the final Hei,
which is the attribute of Malchus;
as is said in the holy Zohar
This is the speculum that does not shine,
through which the work of the world is done," etc.
And this is what they said (Menachos 29b):
"And when Shabbos and Yom Tov come,
which is the Kingdom of Heaven," etc.
And although Binah is only the first Hei,
yet it says "Binah, which is Yud-Kei-Vav."
That is as is stated in the holy Zohar
the mystery of the three Avos
who are united with the only daughter,
and she is crowned with them," etc.;
from the side of three supernal levels:
and she is the bas, the daughter," etc.;
and cessation from all work," etc.
And it says that she is crowned
for the three Avos are a chariot
Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
is a chariot for the attribute of Chochmah,
the two thousand years of Torah,
and it is stated in the Midrash Rabbah
and Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
is a chariot for the attribute of Binah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב קעה, ב)
as is said in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 175b):
and Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
מַבְרִיחַ מִן הַקָּצֶה אֶל הַקָּצֶה (שְׁמוֹת כו, כח)
as is said in the holy Zohar there,
that Yaakov completed the two sides;
that is, the aspect of Da'as,
which is the joining of mind and heart,
as is said in the holy Zohar
and Da'as is the inwardness of Keser Elyon.
And the three meals of Shabbos
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א כו, א)
as is said in the holy Zohar (Zohar I 26a);
הַיּוֹצֵא מֵעֵדֶן לְהַשְׁקוֹת אֶת הַגָּן (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב, י)
"that goes out of Eden to water the garden" (Bereishis 2:10).
for the main thing is Binah,
which is also called the World to Come,
and this is from the holiness of Yitzchak,
that the wisdom enters the depths of the heart:
וְזֶה עַל יְדֵי קְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And this is through the holiness of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
which is a chariot for the attribute of Tiferes, the Vav,
the joining of Chochmah and Binah.
And that is why it says:
נַחְתַּת בִּינָה דְּאִינּוּן יק״ו עַל ה׳
"Binah descends, which is Yud-Kei-Vav, upon the Hei";
that is, the bas, the daughter,
who is crowned with the three Avos
and with the three first Sefiros;
that it should enter the heart:
And it mentioned the Kingdom of Heaven,
as we cited from the holy Zohar
after the pattern of the World to Come;
"I am" with the Exodus from Egypt, etc.;
for there are the ten utterances,
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי תָּגוֹ שֶׁל יוּד
and that is through the crown of the Yud
which shines into Chochmah from Keser Elyon;
and through the aspect of Da'as,
and the spreading of her wings
over the daughter and her camps,

p: "And it is said of the camps of S"M and the Serpent:
וְרָאוּ כָּל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ (דְּבָרִים כח, י)
'And all the peoples of the earth shall see (Devarim 28:10)
that the Name of Hashem is called upon you,
the sign of tefillin and the sign of Shabbos, etc.,
and the sign of the bris;
It mentioned here tefillin and Shabbos;
it is expounded from this pasuk:
"These are the tefillin of the head."
that even one who goes about in tefillin,
the nations of the world are not afraid of him
but it is reported from the Rav,
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be for a blessing,
that he was precise about the wording of the Gemara,
"the tefillin that are in the head,"
in the inwardness of the mind;
and the officer ran after him;
he took them off his head," etc.
that tefillin require a clean body
presumably he fulfilled the mitzvah of tefillin properly;
so why was the officer not afraid of him,
and why did he run after him?
why did he take them off his head
and hold them in his hand,
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים ח, ב)
"Those on a mitzvah errand are not harmed,
but where harm is common it is different,
'And Shmuel said, How can I go?
If Shaul hears, he will kill me.
And Hashem said, Take a heifer,' etc."
Now in truth, what was Shmuel asking,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּצְטַוָּה מִפִּי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לֵילֵךְ
Since he was commanded by the Holy One, blessed be He, to go,
surely it was in Hashem's hand to save him
or to cast fear of him upon Shaul!
a person to give himself over,
and no miracle is done for him;
and sometimes a miracle is done for him;
through which he will be saved.
וְעַל זֶה שָׁאַל שְׁמוּאֵל אֵיךְ אֵלֵךְ
And about this Shmuel asked, "How can I go?"
that is, in what manner shall I go:
or to make some means of being saved.
And the Holy One, blessed be He, answered him
that His will was that he take action and a means of being saved,
And so too the matter with Elisha:
he understood that Hashem Yisbarach's will was
that he make a means of being saved;
and that is why he took them in his hand
and said that they were a dove's wings;
and if no miracle would be done for him,
and they were found to be a dove's wings.
For had it been Hashem Yisbarach's will
fear of him would have fallen upon the officer,
and he would not have run after him.
And this is why the holy Zohar brought
the sign of Shabbos and the sign of tefillin:
דְּבַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (יִתְרוֹ, חֵלֶק ב פט, א)
for in the holy Zohar (Yisro, Zohar II 89a)
נִדְרָשׁ בְּיוֹם הָנִיחַ ה׳ לְךָ וְגוֹ׳
"On the day that Hashem gives you rest," etc.,
is expounded as referring to the day of Shabbos.
Yet how can a person have repose
when he is in the midst of servitude
But Hashem Yisbarach places on Shabbos
repose in the heart of Yisrael,
so that he senses that this is not
the doing of flesh and blood,
but rather it is Hashem Yisbarach's will;
וְזֶהוּ רַק אַשּׁוּר שֵׁבֶט אַפִּי (יְשַׁעְיָה י, ה)
and this is only "Ashur, the rod of My anger" (Yeshayahu 10:5),
"And I will set My throne in Eilam," etc.
that in truth there would fall
the fear of Hashem upon the officer,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר וְרָאוּ וְגוֹ׳ וְיָרְאוּ מִמֶּךָּ
as it says, "And they shall see," etc., "and they shall fear you."
And that he ran after him
that the fear not fall upon him;
and once he ran from before him
and took them off his head,
then the miracle was done for him,
that they were found to be a dove's wings.
upon the camps of S"M and the Serpent,
that it is Hashem Yisbarach's will,
and "Ashur, the rod of My anger";
וְלָכֵן יֵשׁ לוֹ נַיְיחָא בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת
and therefore he has repose on the day of Shabbos,
even one who during the week bears
the yoke of the wicked kingdom;
"the day that Hashem gives you rest," etc.,
that is, he sees that it is from Hashem Yisbarach.
And Shabbos and the sign of the bris:
for Shabbos too is in the mystery of the bris,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א נו, א)
as is said in the holy Zohar (Zohar I 56a).
And this is what it says:
אוֹת תְּפִילִּין וְאוֹת שַׁבָּת וְאוֹת בְּרִית

p: Further, there in the holy Zohar:
"And there is the sign of Shakai,
which is Metatron, the servant," etc.,
who serve in order to receive a reward;
is the gematria of the Name Shakai.
גַּם כֵּן מִשְּׁמוֹתָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
is also one of the Names of the Holy One, blessed be He,
why did it call it a servant
who serve in order to receive a reward?
corresponds to the attribute of Yesod Olam.
And it is stated in the Gemara:
as it is written, 'and for the upright of heart, joy'"
one who fulfills the entire Torah,
even the fine points of Rabbinic mitzvos;
he is not called a tzaddik,
וְכָל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְקַיֵּים דִּבְרֵי חֲכָמִים
"And whoever does not fulfill the words of the Sages
but neither is he called wicked";
"and one who does not fulfill the words of the Sages
but wicked he is not called."
רַק כָּל זְמַן שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ הֶרְגֵּשׁ בַּגּוּף
But as long as he has bodily sensation
that Hashem Yisbarach should illuminate for him.
when he merits uprightness of heart,
then "for the upright of heart, joy."
"One who says, 'This sela is for tzedakah
so that my son may live,
and so that I may merit through it
the life of the World to Come'
And when one acts in order to receive a reward,
though he is a complete tzaddik,
nevertheless he is from the side of a servant,
who acts for the sake of the reward;
and when he refrains from something
that is against his master's will,
it is only from fear of punishment.
But one who merits uprightness of heart
out of love of Hashem Yisbarach,
and when he refrains from evil
it is out of supernal fear.
And just as in the figure of the human form
to which Knesses Yisrael is likened,
And it is stated in the Tikkunim
that Torah with fear and love
וְנִשְׁאַל הָרַב זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה
And the Rav, may the memory of the holy tzaddik be for a blessing, was asked
what root this has in the Gemara;
that it is found explicitly in the Gemara (Pesachim 50b):
כְּתִיב (תְּהִלִּים נז, יא) כִּי גָדוֹל עַד שָׁמַיִם
"It is written (Tehillim 57:11), 'For great unto the heavens,'
וּכְתִיב (תְּהִלִּים קח, ה) כִּי גָדוֹל מֵעַל שָׁמַיִם
and it is written (Tehillim 108:5), 'For great above the heavens';
Here, of those who act for its own sake;
there, of those who act not for its own sake."
That is, when one acts not for its own sake,
and it reaches only "unto the heavens."
no personal interest whatsoever in the body,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא קַמָּא מא, א)
along the lines of what they said in the Gemara (Bava Kamma 41a):
וּבַעַל הַשּׁוֹר נָקִי (שְׁמוֹת כא, כח) וְכוּלֵּי
"'And the owner of the ox is clean' (Shemos 21:28), etc.:
as a person says to his fellow,
'So-and-so came out clean of his property,'
וְאֵין לוֹ בָּהֶם הֲנָאָה שֶׁל כְּלוּם
and has no benefit from them at all"
Elisha was called Ba'al Kenafayim, master of wings,
for he had the two wings,
דְּבְשַׁבָּת אַף מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ זוֹכֶה לָזֶה
that on Shabbos, even one who does not merit this,
and is only in the aspect of a servant,
"For Shabbosos are so called with regard to servants,
'whether as sons or as servants,' etc.;
כִּי לִי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲבָדִים (וַיִּקְרָא כה, נה)
'for unto Me the Children of Yisrael are servants' (Vayikra 25:55),
וְהִיא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה שָׁם)
And this is according to what they said (Rosh Hashanah 4a):
for among the nations of the world,
when they act in order to receive a reward,
whereas Yisrael, who are bound at the root
and "their will is to do Your will," etc.,
or that he may merit the life of the World to Come,
since he intended his own benefit,
for he does not act at all
for the sake of Hashem's commandment,
but intends only his own benefit.
אַף כְּשֶׁעוֹשֶׂה עַל מְנָת לְקַבֵּל פְּרָס
even when one acts in order to receive a reward,
and he is in the aspect of a servant,
nevertheless he is a complete tzaddik,
and he has cessation and repose on Shabbos,
